A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe FAIR-Calib and include matching Appendices A–F. Text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison; all pages except the title and main-results pages render identically.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments on LLaDA and Dream, component ablations, mechanistic diagnostics, and appendix results on additional quantization settings and memory usage.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original benchmark results, ablations, mechanistic diagnostics, and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Algorithm A retain the same teacher probing, frontier/reliability weighting, and off-policy layer-wise calibration procedure. The appendix adaptations are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten evaluation benchmarks, GSM8K probing data, and WikiText2 calibration data. No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain FP, RTN, QuaRot, and FlatQuant comparisons. Appendix Tables A–B retain the same FlatQuant and QDrop-style comparisons; changed boldface does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The W4A4 main evaluations, W3A4 and W8A8 appendix settings, calibration lengths, sample counts, metrics, and decoding policies are unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 retain the same component, probing-budget, and time-weighting ablations. Section 5.4 and Appendices D–E retain identical diagnostic and generalization analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, diagnostic sample counts, variability bands, and fixed-seed information. No uncertainty reporting or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings remain unchanged, including appendix results. Tables 1–2 change font emphasis only; the scores and rankings implied by those scores are identical.

T1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain identical assumptions, KL decompositions, bounds, proofs, and qualifications. Mathematical definitions and appendix derivations are also unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about irreversible-commit instability, the two-stage calibration framework, theoretical justification, and empirical benefits.

C2.justification: Interpretations of error amplification, cross-corpus transferability, and Dream versus LLaDA stability are unchanged. The policy-shift and off-policy domain-mismatch qualifications in Appendix B are retained verbatim.

D1.justification: Algorithm A and Appendices C and F retain the same implementation settings, hyperparameters, calibration procedures, and resource information. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and positioning relative to existing diffusion models and PTQ methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 4 June 2026 to v2 dated 19 July 2026. The paper's prose, terminology, headings, and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 correct boldface emphasis to recognize baseline wins and ties instead of bolding every FAIR-Calib score. Examples include QuaRot's 65.69 versus FAIR-Calib's 62.69 on LLaDA-Base/BoolQ, and FlatQuant's 64.18 versus 64.04 on Dream-Instruct/MMLU. Figures, table structures, captions, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects misleading emphasis in Tables 1–2, making baseline wins and ties already present in v1's numbers easier to recognize. This improves the accuracy of the comparative presentation, while scientific content, evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
